Subject: Quick data check so we can size a dedicated pool for BlueWave

Hi Samir / team —

Great demo yesterday — thanks for walking us through the production flows. To get you an accurate dedicated-pool recommendation I need a short set of operational numbers from your side so our capacity math maps to your sessions and SLOs. If you can confirm the bullets below I’ll circulate two options (cost-optimized vs conservative safety margin) and a one-page runbook for fallbacks.

Can you confirm:
- Peak concurrent requests (users or sessions hitting the model at same time)
- Typical request profile: mean tokens per call, 90th/95th token sizes, and percent of calls that go into long-generation mode (>=512 tokens)
- Required latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for generation path and for cheap short responses
- Any residency/security constraints (we have different region options)

Attached is our preliminary workbook with the fields we need — fill the green column and send back. I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben for the model/ops assumptions.

Hi Logan —

Thanks — answered inline in the workbook you sent (see attached). Summary here so you don’t have to open the sheet:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~420 sessions (we plan for headroom to 500)
- Average tokens per call: 280 tokens
- 95th token size: 920 tokens (about 18% of calls hit long-gen >=512)
- Expected peak QPS: ~90 requests/sec aggregated across all endpoints in peak 1-hr window
- Required SLOs: p50 < 120ms for short responses (<100 tokens), p95 < 420ms for generation path (we can tolerate p99 up to 800ms)
- Data residency: US only (no EU)

We also added a note that some high-priority customers will require guaranteed isolation (that’s why we’re exploring a dedicated pool).

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:30:15 -0800
Subject: BLUEWAVE: draft sizing analysis and trade-offs (please review)

Team —

I ran the numbers from Samir’s workbook and sketched two viable dedicated-pool configurations. High level assumptions: model = open-quant-v1 (production-ish), network RTT accounted for 10ms, average prompt length 280 tokens, 18% long-gen. Benchmarks used: A100 (80GB) single-GPU q4_kernels gives ~1,050 tokens/sec at batch window latency ~120ms; H100 moves that to ~1,900 tps in same config. These are conservative: real-world depends on sequence shape and KV cache hit patterns.

Option A — Cost-optimized (meets SLO at nominal load with small buffer)
- Hardware: 6 x A100 80GB
- Effective aggregate tps (est): 6 * 1,050 = 6,300 tokens/sec
- At peak (90 req/s * avg 280 tokens = 25,200 tokens/sec) -> requires batching across requests; model parallelism + request batching yields effective throughput but observed latency at p95 predicted ~380–420ms under 90 qps with batch window 25ms
- Notes: meets p95 420ms target in most windows but only ~10% headroom; riskier if long-gen bursts co-occur across users

Option B — Safety margin (preferred for SLA-bound customers)
- Hardware: 10 x A100 80GB (or 6 x H100 if we price for H100)
- Effective aggregate tps (est): 10 * 1,050 = 10,500 tokens/sec (or H100 option ~11,400 tps)
- At peak: reserves ~>2x headroom vs observed peak tokens/sec; predicted p95 generation latency ~260–320ms with tail smoothing and smaller batch windows
- Notes: easier to support bursty long-gen windows, allows KV/prefix cache rebuild without impacting p95 for short responses

Other ops notes and mitigations
- Enable prefix caching for common system prompts (reduces token work for repeat calls)
- Use routing policy: route short responses to a lower-cost quantized variant (q4) and route long-gen to the high-capacity pool
- Canary and throttle policy: allow us to shed best-effort traffic under overload rather than impacting SLA customers

Questions for pricing/commit fit: Marissa / Ben — do we want to propose Option B as the default for the initial 12-mo commit with an upsell path for more H100s later? I can produce the math per-month if we agree on the hardware mix.

[Inline: I’ve attached a copy of the workbook with both options tabbed. See 'OptionA' and 'OptionB' sheets.]

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:24:09 -0800
Subject: Re: BLUEWAVE: draft sizing analysis and trade-offs (please review)

Thanks Logan — good work. A couple of operational points to add before we lock Option B in a proposal:

- KV / prefix cache: assume warm cache for ~65% of calls after a steady state; that drops effective token load by ~22% on our numbers. We should reflect a warmed cache scenario and a cold-cache ramp for the first 30 minutes of a new deployment.
- Autoscaling and burst: recommend we keep 20% reserved headroom for short-notice bursts; we can advertise this as an "operational buffer" in the contract to avoid exceptions on 95th-percentile spikes.
- Quantization/variant routing: for cost sensitivity, route <120-token replies to a q4 model on cheaper instances (same pool) but pin VIP customers to the higher-precision variant.

If Marissa/Neha are good with the language I’ll add these bullets to the MAP and hand it to Growth for commitment pricing.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
